title: Harry Boan
used: Harry Boan (1860–1941) opened Boans department store in Perth, Western Australia, in 1895 with his brother (it closed in 1986); married Sophie Bebarfald in 1896 and had four children; member of the Western Australian Legislative Council. No Adelaide business is mentioned.

title: Ulster King of Arms
used: The office of Ulster King of Arms was created in 1552; Nevile Wilkinson held it from 1908 to 1940, after which it was vacant, with a deputy; in 1943 it was joined to Norroy (Norroy and Ulster King of Arms), and heraldry in the Republic passed to the Chief Herald of Ireland at the Genealogical Office.

title: College of Arms
used: Founded by royal charter of Richard III on 2 March 1484 (re-chartered 1555); at 130 Queen Victoria Street, London; thirteen officers: three kings of arms, six heralds and four pursuivants, besides officers extraordinary. James Peill is Garter King of Arms.

title: Rouge Dragon Pursuivant
used: An office of the College of Arms instituted by Henry VII in 1485; the present holder, since 2023, is Phillip Bone (an Oxford DPhil in classics, according to the College's announcement as summarised in search results).

title: Sir Marcus Somerville, 4th Baronet
used: Born 1772, died 11 July 1831; a Whig, MP for County Meath in the Irish House of Commons (1800) and at Westminster until his death; succeeded as 4th Baronet in 1800; married in 1801 Mary Anne Meredyth; father of the 1st Baron Athlumney.

title: Elizabeth Conyngham, Marchioness Conyngham
used: "Thought to be the last mistress of King George IV"; her daughter Lady Maria Harriet Conyngham (1810–1843) married William Somerville, later 1st Baron Athlumney.

title: Thomas Bellingham
used: Thomas Bellingham (1644/45 – 15 September 1721), son of Henry Bellingham and Lucy Sibthorpe: "He was an aide to King William prior to the Battle of the Boyne", his knowledge of the Louth countryside helping the Williamite preparations; Jacobites burned his house at Castlebellingham in 1690.

title: Official Roll of the Baronetage
used: The Roll is maintained for the Lord Chancellor; a claimant must furnish legal evidence of succession; a baronet not on the Roll is not entitled to the title's precedence or to be so described in official documents; in 2020 about 200 baronetcies had no proven holder.

title: Lord Somerville
used: The Scottish Somervilles trace their origin to Sir Gualter (Walter) de Somerville, "a Norman knight and companion of William the Conqueror", rewarded with lands including Whichnour (Wychnor) in Staffordshire and Aston Somerville near Evesham; The Memorie of the Somervilles, written in 1679 by James, 11th Lord Somerville, was published in two volumes in 1815, edited by Sir Walter Scott.

title: Riall (family)
publisher: Landed Estates Database, University of Galway
reliability: Scholarly database; seen only in search results (the page returned an error when fetched).
used: Describes the Rialls as a Quaker family established in Clonmel by the end of the 17th century who became bankers; William Riall of Annerville was a son of Phineas Riall of Heywood. Not read directly.

title: The Somerville family Bible: Captain William Somerville's record of his family, with Tenison Alan Somerville's copy of 1850
publisher: In the narrator's keeping; not published
reliability: A family record kept by the head of the household is among the best evidence for births and deaths before civil registration. This one is known only from a reading aloud in the second recording, transcribed once by speech-to-text, and three dates as heard disagree with the 1897 pedigree, which was drawn from the same family records (see the open question on the family Bible).
used: Read aloud in the second recording (C¶25–34): Captain William's entry of his own birth and marriage and of Eliza's birth and death "at Bayview Avenue in the City of Dublin", and of each of the ten children "as they were born or baptized" (C¶27), with the godparents of the first Eliza (1808), her death at Warrenpoint in 1812 and burial at Clonallan, and the birthplaces Lucan, Newry and Dundalk. An envelope labelled by Cecil B. Rooke holds "one small page of the original family record entered in the family Bible by Captain William Somerville", a "copy of the entire record of Captain William Somerville made by his son T.A. in 1850", and Tenison Alan's own "record of the births of his children" (C¶34).

title: Letters patent confirming the Somerville arms to Elizabeth Mary Somerville and the descendants of Major William Somerville (the original, 1924)
publisher: In the narrator's keeping; not published
reliability: The original grant, with its seal; read aloud in part in the second recording. Its date was not read out; the National Library's catalogue of the register copy dates it 2 April 1924.
used: Read aloud in part (C¶79–86): issued by "Major Sir Nevile Rodwell Wilkinson, Knight Commander of the Royal Victorian Order … Ulster King of Arms, and Principal Herald of All Ireland" on the application of "Elizabeth Mary Somerville of 74 [More]hampton Road in the City of Dublin, only child of Henry Bellingham Somerville, District Inspector, Royal Irish Constabulary, who was great-grandson of William Somerville, Major in His Majesty's Army, second son of Sir James Somerville of the City of Dublin, Baronet, M.P.", confirming arms "long used and borne" by the family but not previously recorded to her and the other descendants of Major William; the shield, crest and motto.

title: Newspaper report of the death of Lord Athlumney (January 1929), a family cutting
publisher: In the narrator's keeping; not published
reliability: A contemporary press report, read aloud; the newspaper's title and date were not read out.
used: Read aloud (C¶91–96): "Lord Athlumney dies at his Irish home", at Somerville, Balrath, Co. Meath; owned 10,000 acres; also Baron Meredyth of the United Kingdom and a baronet; "There is no heir to the barony. Major William A.T.B. Somerville is heir to the baronetcy"; aged 63; Harrow; succeeded his father in 1873; married in 1919 Marjorie Boan, daughter of Mr Boan of Australia; page of honour and ADC to three Viceroys of Ireland; Coldstream Guards and Egyptian Army; ADC to Lord Kitchener; Dongola expedition 1896 (mentioned in despatches; Osmanieh, Medjidie, Sudan medal and two clasps); commanded a battery of machine guns in South Africa; Provost Marshal of London in the Great War.

title: Bellingham Arthur Somerville's genealogical notebooks
publisher: In the narrator's keeping; not published
reliability: Notes made over a lifetime from documents, many lost in 1922, and from what relatives told him; not chronological, and of varying authority.
used: Shown and read from in the second recording (C¶4–11): begun "when he was a boy"; notes going back "to Sir Gualter de Somerville"; on St Audoen's parish, Dublin; and on Dorothea Riall, "third daughter of William Riall of Annerville by his wife, Dorothea Bellingham", first cousin of Tenison Alan Somerville, who married in 1830 Richard Moore of Clonmel.

title: Pedigree rolls prepared for the baronetcy claim (1950s), and the narrator's roll of living descendants
publisher: In the narrator's keeping; not published
reliability: Prepared by the family to support a claim; not independent evidence.
used: Shown in the second recording (C¶177–188): two rolls "prepared in the 1950s … in order to put the claim in", a family tree of Corry Somerville's descendants, and a roll of the living family recording, for example, the interviewer's baptism at St Audoen's in 2006.

title: The narrator's written profiles of the family (in progress, 2020s)
publisher: In the narrator's keeping; not published
reliability: The narrator's own research, with his additions marked in red; unfinished.
used: Shown on screen in the second recording (C¶150–167, 195): profiles of every member of the family in "branches", the first (Major William's descendants) complete and the second (the senior line) well advanced; the profile of Bellingham Arthur is divided into childhood, profession and the Clermont years.

title: Family portraits, miniatures and photographs
publisher: In the narrator's keeping; not published
reliability: Identifications are the narrator's, sometimes from labels on the backs of the pictures; dates of painting not established.
used: Shown in the second recording (C¶236–275): Colonel Thomas Bellingham and a woman the narrator calls his wife "Anna"; one of the two Henry Bellinghams, MPs; Sir Marcus Somerville; John Williams Clinch and his wife; Monique Bâby; an Alan Bellingham; miniatures of Sir James Somerville, 1st Bt, Major William, Captain William and Eliza Bellingham (unfinished); "probably Wicked Alan, son of Henry Bellingham"; Judge Tenison; Daniel O'Connor of Shoreham; a portrait from Maudie Moore's family; and a photograph of Bellingham Arthur's family.
